facts.raw_span: discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla
severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night
denied any recent trauma or history of similar lesions
denied associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms (eg, fever, chills)
3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion that are limited to his right axilla
No other lesions were noted on his skin or mucous membranes
A Wood lamp examination was negative
lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement

concepts.why: The patient presents with discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla, severe pruritus, and no improvement with treatment, which suggests contact dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus are consistent with atopic dermatitis.
The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion is consistent with seborrheic dermatitis.
The patient's biopsy findings of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction and the presence of violaceous, annular patches are consistent with lichen planus.
The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus, and the lack of improvement with treatment, suggest an allergic reaction to deodorant.
The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus are consistent with dyshidrotic eczema.
The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion is consistent with nummular dermatitis.
The patient's biopsy findings of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction and the presence of violaceous, annular patches are consistent with psoriasis.

rationales.F01: The presence of discrete, dark red, circular lesions is more typical of lichen planus.

rationales.F03: The absence of recent trauma or history of similar lesions makes contact dermatitis less likely.
rationales.F05: The presence of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches is more typical of lichen planus.
rationales.F06: The absence of other lesions on the skin or mucous membranes makes atopic dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, and psoriasis less likely.
rationales.F08: The presence of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction is a hallmark of lichen planus.
rationales.F09: The lack of response to treatment with hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant suggests a condition that is not easily treatable with these methods.
